title: Man accused of kidnapping woman he met on dating app, keeping her captive in attic for weeks
text:
MALDEN, Mass. (WFXT) - A Massachusetts man is being held without bail after he pleaded not guilty to keeping a woman he reportedly met on a dating app captive in an attic for weeks.
Jordende Piere, 29, pleaded not guilty to multiple charges in court Sept. 25 after he was arrested in a human trafficking investigation. He was ordered held without bail.
Prosecutors say Piere is accused of keeping a woman in the attic of a Malden apartment building for weeks, where authorities say she was sexually abused and living in poor conditions. The woman had not eaten, was covered in scabs and was using a bucket as a toilet, according to prosecutors.
Malden Police Chief Marc Gatcomb said the investigation began when an officer noticed something out of place at the apartment building, which led officers to the victim.
The woman told police she met Piere on a dating app. Investigators say he forced her to have sex with him and arranged sexual encounters with other people.
Gatcomb says the case is a reminder that human trafficking can be happening anywhere.
“[These cases] are very disturbing. There are a lot of moving parts to them. Sometimes, these types of crimes are hidden in plain sight, right under your noses in neighborhoods, hotels and whatnot,” he said.
Piere is charged with kidnapping, human trafficking and indecent assault and battery on a person over 14. Authorities say he was on release at the time of his arrest on assault and battery and weapons charges out of Somerville.
Piere is scheduled to return to court Tuesday.
Police say the investigation is ongoing, and there could be more charges involving other people.

title: Family of Late Edgecomb Firefighter Continues His Legacy with Nonprofit Organization
text:
Members of fire departments in Lincoln County gathered at the Edgecomb Fire Department on Saturday, Sept. 26 to pick up equipment donated by a nonprofit foundation formed to honor the founders’ late son.
The Gavin Martin Foundation is dedicated to honoring the legacy of Gavin Martin, a 21-year-old Edgecomb firefighter who died in a car crash in December 2025. At the Sept. 26 event, Monika and Joel Martin said they wanted to follow their son’s example of giving back and created a foundation to help the organizations and communities he loved.
“Having other people say his name keeps him alive for us,” Monika Martin said.
Haley Gifford, a member of the foundation’s board and one of Gavin Martin’s older cousins, said the nonprofit came together after the family was looking for a way to remember him. Originally from Verona, N.J., Gavin Martin had spent time volunteering for the fire department there and after college, eventually joined the Edgecomb Fire Department. Gifford said the family has a house in the town where Gavin Martin moved into after college.
“Really supporting those dreams that he had as a young adult and being able to give back to the first responders and young people with their trades is really where the idea came from, and just continuing his name,” Gifford said.
When the nonprofit was first started earlier this year, Gifford said initiatives included a blood drive and other community events in both Maine and New Jersey. In the past couple of months, the organization dedicated a new field where Gavin Martin played baseball in New Jersey and donated to other areas he cared about.
In June, the organization gave out scholarships to graduating students in both New Jersey and Maine. Students from Boothbay Regional High School, Wiscasset Middle High School, Lincoln Academy, and Medomak Valley High School were tasked with writing about how they display generosity in their daily lives. The organization gave out a total of $15,000 in scholarships, with students getting around $1,000 to $1,500 each.
The biggest event the organization has held so far was a Midcoast fire training weekend in August at the Boothbay Fire Department’s training center. Gifford said the training welcomed firefighters from Maine and New Jersey, as well as others from around New England. The training brought in instructors and included ropes training, extrication activities, and other hands-on practice.
The Edgecomb Fire Department offered its firehouse for lectures and the Wiscasset Fire Department hosted other trainings.
Gifford said the Sept. 26 event was a thank-you for the participating departments, which included the towns of Alna, Boothbay, Boothbay Harbor, Edgecomb, South Bristol, and Wiscasset. The foundation purchased equipment used in the training so the participating departments didn’t have to pay for it themselves.
“A lot of the attendees really didn’t know what to expect, but they were so thankful, so grateful about how great it was,” Gifford said. “Somebody actually recently emailed us and said that they continued to talk about the weekend and actually they were able to use some of the new skills they had at a recent extrication.”
The Edgecomb community that once rallied around Gavin Martin when he moved to the town alone as a young person has now rallied around his parents, both Monika and Joel Martin said.
Beyond being a first responder, Gavin Martin also had a passion for the trades. Monika Martin said her son had a background in engineering, recalling how he played with Lego blocks all of his life and enjoyed building things.
Gavin Martin graduated from Central Maine Community College and near the end of his time in school, he worked numerous jobs. His mother said he was looking for something in project management or construction, something hands-on. After not enjoying a job mowing lawns, Monika Martin said Gavin Martin went on to found his own landscaping company.
Gavin Martin also started working for the Waldoboro Public Works Department. Monika Martin said during this time, her son developed a close working relationship with Town Manager Julie Keizer.
“When we think about him, like he always helps, even though he was up here by himself,” Monika Martin said. “He had neighbors, but some of them were way older than him and he would always check in and make sure things were going on. He was always giving back.”
After serving in their fire department back home in New Jersey, Joel Martin said he recently joined Edgecomb’s department. He said the goal is to move to Maine once their daughter graduates high school.
“We have plans to be here full time, but a little painful without Gavin running around, so we’ll figure it out,” Joel Martin said.
Edgecomb Fire Chief Roy Potter said he watched Gavin Martin grow up and that his loss affected the department greatly.
Since the Gavin Martin Foundation was founded, Potter said the work the organization has done to benefit fire departments has been “incredible,” especially with the decline in volunteerism around the state. He used the example of his department, which has 17 members, three of whom are over the age of 60 and two are over the age of 70.
Having opportunities to go to a training like the one in August helps with accessibility for those interested in becoming a firefighter, Potter said. Not only were participants able to learn more about hands-on work, they were able to collaborate with members of other departments.
As the Gavin Martin Foundation heads toward one year as a nonprofit organization, Joel Martin said they plan on coordinating more training events and other ways to give back to the communities his son loved. He said he is currently in conversation with the state on getting funding to rejuvenate the fire training center in Wiscasset.
“The best part about it is it keeps Gavin’s legacy going,” Potter said.
For more information about the Gavin Martin Foundation, email [email protected] or go to gavinmartinfoundation.org.

What's the MLB rule when the ball hits the roof?
text:
What's the MLB rule when the ball hits the roof?
It may be one of the craziest moments you've ever seen in a Brewers game.
What's the MLB rule when the ball hits the roof?
It may be one of the craziest moments you've ever seen in a Brewers game.
The Brewers may have had one of their wildest moments ever.
Ty France, up to the plate for the Padres with one out in the ninth inning of a 3-2 game and a runner on first, sends a ball high into the sky — and it hits the cables at the top of American Family Field's roof.
Jackson Chourio finds his way under the ball and catches it for the second out.
One out later, the Brewers secured Game 1 in their NLDS series with the Padres on Saturday night.
If the roof had been open, it appeared the ball would have found its way into the stands for a two-run homer and lifted the Padres to a 4-3 lead.
France’s drive left his bat at 105.3 mph with a 49-degree launch angle. It was caught 325 feet from home plate.
Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy thought the ball would have hooked foul if it didn’t ricochet off the roof.
“It was going to be a foul ball, for sure. I’m standing right on that line,” Murphy said. “A hitter that talented, they would have liked to have that hitter back up there with another strike.”
So what's the rule?
According to MLB.com's Adam McCalvy, the ballpark's ground rules say if a ball hits the roof, roof truss or roof cable over fair territory, it is considered in play. That's exactly what happened, and Chourio caught the ball for the out.
If the ball hit the roof over fair territory and landed in foul territory, it would have been a foul ball. And if it hit the roof over foul territory, it would be considered a dead ball.
The Padres challenged the call, arguing it should have been a dead ball. The umpires confirmed the original call of an out on the field was correct.
Response from Padres
“We joked about it at the umpire meeting today about what would happen if the ball hit the roof. And it was unlikely, but it happened,” San Diego manager Craig Stammen said. “Unfortunately, a bad break for us. Looked like it was a possible home run. Just didn’t go our way.”
This has happened before
According to McCalvy, this has happened at least two other times in Brewer's history.
- 2008: Game 4 of the NLDS against the Philadelphia Phillies
- 2018: April game against the Cincinnati Reds
In all three instances, the ball was caught by a Brewer.
This article contains information from The Associated Press.

title: US Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted by a suspected terror attack
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base.
The bombers were redeployed back to their home bases in the United States, according to a Pentagon official who was not authorized to discuss sensitive military movements and spoke Sunday on condition of anonymity.
Aviation watchers such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers fly out of the base on Sunday.
The move comes as President Donald Trump weighs options for his war on Iran — including new strikes — despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks.
“We have decisions that I’ll make about Iran. Iran’s been decimated. So the only question is — it’ll either be the easy way, or the hard way,” Trump told reporters on Saturday as he left the White House for a rally in Ohio.
A dual British-Iranian national was arrested in central London last week on suspicion of plotting a terror attack, following a security incident at RAF Fairford in late September. In total, six people have been taken into custody and then released on bail during the investigation.
British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran. Iran has denied involvement. It has previously said it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.
U.K. officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arson and other attacks in Britain and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community and intended to sow fear. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.
RAF Fairford, located 100 miles (160 kilometers) west of London, has been used by American bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East.
The U.S. military still maintains a sizable presence in the Middle East. On Thursday, a U.S. official said the recently deployed USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier, as well as the USS Malkin Island amphibious readiness group — a group of ships that together carry over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines — are heading for the region. The official said the move could result in three carriers in the region as early as the end of October.

title: Patriots stun Buffalo with late game heroics
text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, including Efton Chism’s one-handed catch with 1:50 remaining, and the New England Patriots defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26 on Sunday.
Romeo Doubs had touchdown catches of 2 and 14 yards, and Rhamondre Stevenson scored on a 1-yard run.
Though Maye’s turnover troubles continued with an interception and a lost fumble in the first half, the third-year starter was sharp in the final minutes after New England fell behind 26-21.
Maye’s 23-yard TD pass to Chism came on third-and-5, with the receiver bringing in the ball with his right hand and maintaining control in the end zone. Maye then hit Stevenson for the 2-point conversion.
Despite having a minute left and the ball at their 40, Josh Allen turned overly aggressive. On second-and-6, he spun out of Dre’Mont Jones’ sack attempt, stepped up in the pocket and went deep only to have his underthrown pass intended for Josh Palmer intercepted by Craig Woodson.
Taking over at the Patriots 19, Maye put the finishing touches on the win by rolling to his right and lobbing a 12-yard pass to Hunter Henry in allowing the Patriots to run out the clock.
The Patriots improved to 2-2 and for once put aside questions about a sputtering and turnover-prone offense.
The Bills, meantime, dropped to 3-1 in Buffalo’s first loss at its new Highmark Stadium, and first under new coach Joe Brady.
Maye finished 22 of 37 for 269 yards in overcoming the criticism he’s faced in opening the season by combining for six interceptions and a lost fumble in his first three starts. The lost fumble, recovered by the Buffalo at its 30, was on Maye, who lost the ball as Bills tackle Ed Oliver shoved an offensive lineman into him.
The interception, however, was on Doubs, who made the catch and in the process spun around and lost control of the ball, which sailed into the hands of cornerback Dee Alford.
The Bills had their sloppy moments, too, a week after committing five turnovers in a 24-16 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
Receiver Khalil Shakir lost a fumble, in addition to Allen’s interception — his third of the season. Allen finished 23 of 33 for 253 yards, including a 34-yard go-ahead touchdown to Keon Coleman with 4:27 remaining. The touchdown put Buffalo up 26-21, but the 2-point conversion attempt failed when Palmer never looked for Allen’s pass directed his way.
Allen also scored on a 2-yard run, while James Cook scored on an 8-yard run.
The Bills were limited to 340 total yards and 19 first downs, both season lows, and resembled nothing like the high-powered unit that opened the season combining for 855 yards and 77 points.
The outing was a breakthrough for the Patriots’ slumbering offense, which posted season highs with 405 yards and 26 first downs. New England’s defense also rallied in containing the Bills despite missing its top cornerback Christian Gonzalez and starting defensive tackle Christian Barmore because of shoulder injuries.
ALLEN MILESTONES
Allen’s 2-yard touchdown run to tie the game at 14 with one minute left in the first half was his 88th career from scrimmage (rushing/receiving) to break the team record held by Hall of Famers Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed. It was also Allen’s 86th TD rushing, moving him into a tie with Priest Holmes for 16th place on the NFL’s career list.
INJURIES
Patriots: WR Mack Hollins hurt his calf.
Bills: WR DJ Moore did not return after hurting his shoulder attempting to make a diving catch in the second quarter. DT Ed Oliver left in the third quarter with a knee injury. And a secondary already missing Christian Benford (toe), lost Dee Alford to an ankle injury in the second half.
UP NEXT
Patriots: host the Las Vegas on Sunday.
Bills: at the Los Angeles Rams on “Monday Night Football” on Oct. 12
